name: Kenneth Lay

summary.text: Kenneth Lay was the founder and chairman of Enron Corporation. On May 25, 2006 a Houston jury found him guilty of six counts of conspiracy and fraud, and Judge Sim Lake found him guilty of four further counts of bank fraud and false statements in a separate bench trial. Lay died on July 5, 2006, before sentencing, and on October 17, 2006 Judge Lake vacated the convictions and dismissed the indictment under the doctrine of abatement, which also removed the government's ability to seize his estate's assets for restitution through the criminal case.

facts.claim: On October 17, 2006 Judge Simeon T. Lake III vacated Lay's convictions and dismissed the indictment because his death during the appeal period abated the judgment; the Justice Department had asked the judge to defer so Congress could consider changing the abatement doctrine.
facts.quote: Judge Simeon T. Lake III issued a short order on Tuesday noting that "The indictment against Kenneth L. Lay is dismissed."

sources.title: Judge throws out convictions of Enron's Lay

facts.claim: With the conviction vacated, the government lost the ability to seize property of the Lay estate through the criminal case to compensate Enron victims; the judge also denied a victim's request for a restitution order, and Lay's lawyer said civil claims against the estate could still proceed.
facts.quote: With the vacated conviction, the federal government now has no means of seizing property controlled by the Lay estate to compensate victims of the Enron collapse.
